title: Congressman Harrigan co-leads bipartisan bill on parental screen time controls
text:
Congressman Harrigan co-leads bipartisan bill on parental screen time controls
Congressman Pat Harrigan of North Carolina joined Congressman George Whitesides of California in introducing the Tracking Online Time And Limits Screen Time (TOTAL Screen Time) Act, bipartisan legislation directing the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop a voluntary technical standard for parental screen time controls, according to a July 15 statement.
Harrigan said, "Parents know exactly how frustrating this is. You can set limits on your child's phone, but then they move to a tablet, a gaming console, or the TV and you're right back where you started. The technology already exists to help families manage screen time, it just doesn't work together. This bill brings everyone to the table to develop one voluntary standard that gives parents a simple, consistent way to manage screen time across devices without sacrificing privacy or creating another government mandate."
The TOTAL Screen Time Act aims not to create new federal regulations but instead brings together technology companies, child safety advocates, medical professionals, privacy experts, and standards organizations. The purpose is to develop a voluntary cross-platform technical standard so parents can set one limit that works across phones, tablets, computers, gaming consoles, televisions and other devices while protecting cybersecurity and avoiding centralized databases of children's activity.
Harrigan will continue working with colleagues from both parties on solutions designed to strengthen families and protect children online.
In 2024 Pat Harrigan defeated Ralph R. Scott Jr., winning 57.5% of the vote in the general election, according to the office of Congressman Pat Harrigan.
